![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14217341/assets/270b7c6ff796937603596f26e70886f41438ce87c043d3a1b4fc221398b8692f.png)

 

The phase portrait for a system of linear differential equations whose matrix has two real, distinct eigenvalues is shown above.
The eigenvalues of the system's matrix are $\lambda_1$ and $\lambda_2,$ for which the corresponding eigenvectors are $\mathbf{v}_1 = [-1, \ 1]^T$ and $\mathbf{v}_2 = [1, \ 0]^T,$ respectively. 

Identify the relations between $\lambda_1,$ $\lambda_2,$ and $0.$
question.worked_solution:
The straight-line solutions of the system have the form
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14217341/assets/0c4b7d443c58e6720389306e73eb4e5e1934cfb7359221f36fb43ceb3e91e501.svg)

The line that passes through the origin and is parallel to ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14217341/assets/3244f8128366a3f7f4ae3e41cd9323b1712f9587943f9fb2de54ee0c458feedf.svg) has the equation 

$$
y= -x,
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14217341/assets/d241239c6475fbcf9559c2fcbbb8ca2805a6692fd1a9b3966fe8b38441075a4d.png)

The tangents along this line are pointing away from the origin, meaning that the solutions of the form 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14217341/assets/c3ac6997c0e8580f8d91b88578a02043ca495e99e3ea67bdf91b3eab9eb43d98.svg)
must approach infinity as $t \to \infty.$ So, we must have $\lambda_1 >  0.$

The line that passes through the origin and is parallel to ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14217341/assets/77200c9fefd57e0b82b796072e07411f5fe10c91185d7d8f665f7ef6c3f54360.svg) has the equation 

$$
y= 0,
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14217341/assets/fb40117d63e76b2b2db59313b173b04a9a23ef2a28493a5041584e4c7c60c67d.png)

The tangents along this line are pointing away from the origin, meaning that the solutions of the form 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14217341/assets/0ce3220f2cd013daba6b1f44f88d2834021b44ba877980f5ec47df7bc52396ce.svg)
must approach infinity as $t \to \infty.$ So, we must have $\lambda_2 > 0.$

So, for this particular system, both eigenvalues are positive. The dominant eigenvalue is the one with the greatest magnitude.

Now, since the solutions become parallel to the straight-line solution containing the vector $\mathbf{v}_2$ as they move away from the origin, the dominant eigenvalue is $\lambda_2.$

Therefore, $\lambda_2 > \lambda_1 > 0.$
